exposure: factors contributing to caesarean section rates (e.g., previous CS, induced labour, nulliparity, multiparity, breech, multiple pregnancies, preterm deliveries)
outcome: distribution of CS rates across Robson groups
cohort: All live and stillbirths with a birth weight >= 500g or gestational age >= 28 weeks delivered at a tertiary care hospital.
finding: The study found a high overall caesarean section rate of 53.95%, with Group 5 (previous CS) and Group 2 (nulliparous, induced or pre-labour CS) contributing the most.
mod_finding: The study suggested promoting vaginal birth after caesarean (VBAC) and refining induction protocols as strategies to reduce CS rates.
